description: Start a background audit of the whole knowledge corpus and return a receipt immediately; the findings are written to a timestamped Markdown report, not returned. The audit walks every *.retrieval_test.yaml companion file under corpus_root and runs the per-article retrieval test against each. Where test_retrieval evaluates a single article, this audits the whole corpus, which takes many minutes. Each article's target queries are judged within its own knowledge base and its forbidden queries are judged across every active knowledge base (the ratified split scope) -- neither check kind means anything under the other's scope. The report lists DRIFT when a target query no longer ranks an article within its min_rank, OVERREACH when a forbidden query ranks an article better than its forbidden_min_rank, STALE_PROCESS_KEY when an asserted process key no longer resolves in the live registry, and LEGACY_KEY when a companion still declares a retired yaml key (e.g. non_target_queries) whose claims go silently unenforced. Only articles in active knowledge bases are audited; active_knowledge_bases narrows that to a subset of the active set. The receipt says started, or already_running when a prior pass is still in flight, and names the report_dir where the new report will appear.
embedding_description: Start a batch sweep of the retrieval health of the entire knowledge corpus in the background: walk every retrieval_test.yaml companion across all active knowledge bases, run each article's gate under its own-KB/cross-KB split scope, and write the findings to one timestamped Markdown report. Returns a started or already-running receipt at once, not the findings. This is the corpus-wide hygiene job. Use to catch drift, overreach, stale process keys, or retired companion yaml keys everywhere, not to check a single article.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Corpus retrieval audit started in the background
result_processor_customizations.result_description: A receipt: audit is 'started' or 'already_running', and report_dir is the directory the timestamped Markdown report will be written into when the pass finishes, many minutes later
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report that the audit is running in the background, not that it has finished. There are no findings in this result; do not invent any. Name report_dir so the reader knows where the report will appear.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Read the newest Markdown report under report_dir once the pass has finished, then act on its findings: for each DRIFT tune the article's embedding_description or retire a superseded article; for each OVERREACH narrow the embedding_description; for each STALE_PROCESS_KEY update the article to the current process key; for each LEGACY_KEY rename the companion yaml's retired key to its stated replacement. Do not start another audit while one is already_running.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Auditing knowledge base retrieval across the corpus. audit_retrieval_corpus accepts {corpus_root?, report_dir?, active_knowledge_bases?, fail_fast?}.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: arguments do not conform to the schema. ValueError: a requested knowledge base is not active. RuntimeError: the knowledge base root is not configured. A malformed retrieval_test.yaml fails inside the background pass and is logged there, not returned here.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Verify any active_knowledge_bases entries name currently active knowledge bases, then retry.
